title: fix(cli): the organization-ownership ceremony reads its dialect once, through metadata-core's shared resolver, and refuses an unresolved one before any statement
body:
Fixes #23558
Clause-②: yes (widening)

The grade is `yes (widening)` because this PR exports one resolver from `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `dialectOfDriver`, so the ceremony can share it. The claim graded the card `no` unless that export was added, and it was added. No existing export answered a driver's dialect.

## What changed

`os migrate organization-ownership` (the plan and `--apply`) now reads its SQL dialect once, from the stack's driver, before either arm runs a statement. It uses the resolver that metadata-core's legacy-row reader uses: the driver's `dialectName` first, then a recognised `config.client` string.

Anything else is refused with `driver-unsupported` and exit 1, and no statement runs. That covers a client class with no recognised `dialectName`, an unrecognised client string, `dialectName: 'unknown'`, and a driver with no dialect at all. The refusal names the driver: its name, its `dialectName`, and its client string or client class name.

- `packages/metadata-core/src/legacy-organization-row.ts`: `dialectOfDriver` is exported. Its behaviour is unchanged, and its doc comment says who shares it.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts`:
  - `dialectOf`, which read the client string only, is replaced by `ceremonyDialectOf(driver)`. It calls the shared resolver and throws the refusal.
  - `PlanReader` carries the resolved `dialect`. `client` stays as the plan file's record, and only when it is a string.
  - The plan no longer derives a dialect itself, and its catalog statement is keyed on the resolved dialect.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts`: the `dialect ?? 'sqlite'` default is gone. The apply takes the executor's resolved dialect.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts`:
  - Both arms call `ceremonyDialectOf(stack.driver)` right after the raw-seam check, before any statement. In `--apply` this is also before the ledger check.
  - The template lookup's `dialectOf(executor.client) ?? 'sqlite'` is gone.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/cli` patch, `@objectstack/metadata-core` minor.

## Premise check against `main` (`f7cd580bff`)

- **The card's harm does not happen on `main`.** The card said "the ceremony would then build SQLite-dialect raw SQL against a PostgreSQL or MySQL database". It would not. Both arms run the plan step first, and the plan's `dialectOf(String(client))` returned null for a client class (stringified) and for an unrecognised string. So the plan refused with `driver-unsupported` before any statement.
  - The apply's `?? 'sqlite'` and the template lookup's `?? 'sqlite'` were reached only after the plan had resolved the same client to a dialect, so neither ever applied.
  - What was live: the refusal printed a client class's whole source text as the driver's name, and three readers each kept their own copy of the resolution.
  - This PR still does what the card's Wanted lines ask: one shared resolver, a refusal naming the driver before any statement, and no SQLite default left.
- **Hypothesis (a), falsified in part.** `resolvePlannedDriverExec` reads no `config.client`; it only picks `execute` or `raw`. In that module the string-only read is `readPhysicalTableNames`, which belongs to `os migrate plan`'s unmanaged-table sweep. The ceremony never calls it. It is left unchanged (see Acceptance notes).
- **Hypothesis (b).** metadata-core's `dialectOfDriver` / `dialectOfName` were not exported, and no exported entry in the repository answers a driver's dialect this way. That is why there is one export.
- **Hypothesis (c).** The refusal happens once, at the command, where the driver is first read. The utils take the resolved dialect.

## No-regression guard: every in-repo driver, measured

Each driver was constructed through the shared datasource factory (`createDefaultDatasourceDriverFactory`) or the runtime's Turso factory, from the build of `0fc3ae2575`. No driver package is touched by this PR. The `main` column is the command's own expression, `dialectOf(String(config.client))`.

| driver path | `name` | `dialectName` | `config.client` | `main` | shared resolver |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SqlDriver on better-sqlite3 | `com.objectstack.driver.sql` | `sqlite` | `'better-sqlite3'` | sqlite | sqlite |
| SqliteWasmDriver | `com.objectstack.driver.sqlite-wasm` | `sqlite` | class `Client_WasmSqlite2` | refused | sqlite |
| SqlDriver on pg | `com.objectstack.driver.sql` | `postgres` | `'pg'` | postgres | postgres |
| SqlDriver on mysql2 | `com.objectstack.driver.sql` | `mysql` | `'mysql2'` | mysql | mysql |
| TursoDriver, remote `libsql://` | `com.objectstack.driver.turso` | `sqlite` | `'better-sqlite3'` | sqlite | sqlite |
| TursoDriver, `file:` | `com.objectstack.driver.turso` | `sqlite` | `'better-sqlite3'` | sqlite | sqlite |

Every driver that ran the ceremony before still runs it.

SqliteWasmDriver never reaches the resolver through the command today. It was measured through the CLI at `91084b5d5e`: `os migrate organization-ownership --database-url wasm-sqlite://FILE --json` answers `{"error":"plan_refused","reason":"driver-unsupported","detail":"no SQL driver with a raw-SQL seam is active"}`. That is the same answer `main` gives. The schema boot's SQL-driver lookup does not include the service name that driver registers under, so `stack.driver` is null. This is reported as a finding and not fixed here.

The SQLite path was also run through the CLI at `f9f69beda5`: `--database-url FILE` (better-sqlite3) writes the plan, records `"client": "better-sqlite3"`, and exits 0.

**NOT MEASURED:** a live PostgreSQL or MySQL run of the ceremony. Both shapes were measured on constructed drivers, and the command pins assert that each one's first statement is its own dialect's catalog read.

## Tests

- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.dialect.test.ts` (new, `unit` tier):
  - Five refused shapes, each in both arms: a client class with no `dialectName`; a client class as `SqlDriver` answers it (`dialectName: 'unknown'`); an unrecognised client string (`oracledb`); `dialectName: 'unknown'` beside `pg`; no `dialectName` and no client.
  - Each one checks: `plan_refused` / `apply_refused`, reason `driver-unsupported`, a detail that names the driver, exit 1, zero statements, no plan file, and the apply step never called.
  - A client class is named, and its source is never printed.
  - Six proceeding shapes: each in-repo driver's measured shape, plus a driver with only a recognised client string. Each one's first statement is its dialect's catalog read.
  - `--apply` hands the executor `dialect`, and `client` only when it is a string.
- `packages/metadata-core/src/legacy-organization-row.test.ts`: the exported `dialectOfDriver`, nine rows. `dialectName` first; a client string when there is no `dialectName`; `'unresolved'` for a client class, an unknown string, and `dialectName: 'unknown'` beside `pg`; `'none'` for no dialect and no driver.
- `organization-ownership-plan.integration.test.ts`: the `oracledb` refusal now pins that the dialect is refused before the plan issues any statement.
- The other readers and executors in the ceremony's tests (`organization-ownership-apply.test.ts:60`, `...served-catalog.integration.test.ts`, `...host-supplement.integration.test.ts`) gain `dialect: 'sqlite'`.

Runs on `107a7a923c`, the final head, after merging `main` at `edac2183c0`, which brings in PR #23624's hunks in the same files. The merge was clean, and was followed by `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and a rebuild of the cli closure.

- `@objectstack/cli` unit project, by path (`organization-ownership.dialect`, `unmanaged-tables`, `organization-ownership.apply-flags`, `organization-ownership-inventory`): 4 files, 90 tests passed.
- `@objectstack/cli` integration project, by path (the plan, apply, served-catalog, host-supplement, column-drops, unmanaged-tables and meta-stored-legacy-organization suites, and the command's fate-supplement, occupancy and journal-mode suites): 10 files, 148 tests passed. This layer was run locally because the diff edits integration-tier files.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` and `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-core typecheck`: exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-core test`: 18 files, 728 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit` (the whole unit layer): 290 of 291 files and 4341 of 4342 tests passed. The one red was `boot-preparation-parity.test.ts > every SERVE_ONLY entry is still used by serve.ts`, a 5000 ms timeout (5160 ms) on a shared box while the gate battery ran beside it. The diff touches neither that file nor `serve.ts`. Re-run alone on the same head: 37 of 37 passed.

## Ablation (one-off proofs, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with an `EXIT INT TERM` restore trap)

Both mutated subjects are `packages/cli/src`, resolved relatively, and metadata-core is aliased to `src` in the cli vitest config, so no `dist/` is involved.

**The SQLite fallback restored in `ceremonyDialectOf`, on `107a7a923c`.** The anchor `if (… ) return dialect;` was replaced with `return … ? dialect : 'sqlite';`. On disk: injected 1, anchor 0; blob `25cf4a26b487` became `476f0e239e7b`.
- The command pins went 11 red / 8 green. Every refused shape went red in both arms, plus the class-naming pin. All proceeding pins stayed green.
- The plan integration suite went 1 red / 11 green: the `oracledb` pin.
- Restored: blob equals HEAD (`25cf4a26b487`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The same result held on `91084b5d5e`.

## Gates

Local, on `107a7a923c`:

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 67 commands from the merge base `edac2183c`, with no stale-tree warning. All 67 were run, and each exit code was captured before any pipe: **67 of 67 exit 0**.
- `--ran` reconciliation: "67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN", exit 0.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage` and `check:i18n-walk-parity` need build output beyond the cli closure. They were measured after building their named prerequisite closures (the CLI, the examples, and the plugins and services they extract). On the pre-merge head they first answered exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) and were re-run green.
- Ratchet families in that set: `check:type-check-coverage` and `check:type-check-debt`, exit 0.
- `pnpm lint` narrowed to the 10 changed `.ts` files: `eslint --no-inline-config` on them, exit 0, no output. The full repo scan is CI's `Lint & Repo Gates`.
- Control-byte self-scan of the changed files and the changeset: no hits.

## Acceptance notes

- **`os migrate` finds no SQL driver on a `wasm-sqlite://` or `*.wasm.db` database.** The schema boot looks a SQL driver up by `SQL_DRIVER_SERVICES` in `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts` (`driver.com.objectstack.driver.sql`, `driver.com.objectstack.driver.turso`, `driver.sql`). SqliteWasmDriver registers under none of them. So the ceremony refuses a SQLite database with "No SQL driver with a raw-SQL seam is active … The ceremony supports SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL." This was measured through the CLI (above). It is reported to the seat as a finding and is not fixed here, because `schema-migrate.ts` is outside this claim.
- **`os migrate plan`'s unmanaged-table sweep still reads `config.client` as a string only** (`readPhysicalTableNames`, `packages/cli/src/utils/unmanaged-tables.ts`). It is the only remaining string-only reader in the cli. It has no reach today: its drivers come from the same lookup, which never plans SqliteWasmDriver. Carrier: none.
- **`packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts` keeps a third copy of the resolver.** In that copy, an unrecognised `dialectName` falls through to the client string. No in-repo driver reaches the difference: `SqlDriver` answers `'unknown'` only for a client that the same three spelling sets do not recognise. Carrier: none.
- Unchanged: `organization-ownership-plan.ts:181`, `organization-ownership-grants.ts`, and the apply test's `:1979`, which belong to PR #23624; and `packages/drivers/**`.
